inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,077 normalized lines. The article develops resonance as a common extremal-value mechanism in three settings: zeta on the critical line, quadratic Dirichlet central values, and holomorphic cusp-form central values. Its reusable content is the conversion of an extremum problem into a ratio of a mixed moment to a resonator norm, diagonal extraction under a length constraint, multiplicative coefficient design and Rankin-tail control, and sign changes in those coefficients to select large versus small family values. The text layer preserves the prose and proof architecture, but displayed formulas have spacing and symbol-order degradation and must be checked against the retained PDF before formula-exact reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction and theorem panel
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the zeta, quadratic-character, and cusp-form extreme-value results; motivates resonance, distributional expectations, portability, and limitations.

sections_inspected.label: Zeta resonance moments and coefficient optimization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Diagonalizes the two smoothed moments and proves the lower and upper bounds for the resulting finite quadratic-form optimization.

sections_inspected.label: Zeta maximum and frequency conclusions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Converts the optimized quotient into a maximum and into lower bounds for the measure of large-value sets in two regimes.

sections_inspected.label: Quadratic Dirichlet setup and asymptotic moments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds a character-valued resonator, isolates square contributions, applies an approximate functional equation, and states the signed Euler-product asymptotics.

sections_inspected.label: Quadratic Dirichlet proposition proof
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Controls truncations, parametrizes the square constraint, evaluates the Mellin residue, factors the main term, and bounds tails.

sections_inspected.label: Cusp-form family adaptation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses harmonic weights, Petersson orthogonality, an approximate functional equation, and Hecke relations to obtain a resonant family quotient and both signs of extremity.

sections_inspected.label: References and affiliation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic and author-contact material; no new source-local mathematical mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Zeta large-value and frequency target
accepted_units.why_material: States both the pointwise extreme-value lower bound and the uniform lower bound for the measure of a large-value set, fixing the two outputs the resonance construction must deliver.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical comparison and heuristic scale are developed later at lines 33-89.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose and parameter range are readable, but radicals, fractions, and nested logarithms in the displayed bounds require verification against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Gaussian-value heuristic and the unresolved extreme scale
accepted_units.why_material: Connects Selberg's approximately Gaussian law for log absolute zeta to a predicted tail measure and much larger extreme scale, while contrasting that heuristic with known conditional upper bounds in different deviation ranges.
accepted_units.context_note: This is motivation, not a proof of the conjectured maximum scale; the source explicitly presents it as a suggestion conditional on tail persistence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-grounded; exact constants and deviation ranges in formulas should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Resonance as a mixed-moment quotient
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a Dirichlet-polynomial resonator, defines its norm and its mixed moment with zeta, bounds the maximum by their ratio, and observes that evaluation turns coefficient choice into optimization of two quadratic forms. This is the paper's transferable conceptual core.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact diagonal evaluations and admissible resonator length begin at line 195.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The inequality and moment definitions are formula-dependent and need PDF verification, while their conceptual relation is clear in the extracted prose.

accepted_units.title: Large and small quadratic Dirichlet central values
accepted_units.why_material: States matched large- and small-value conclusions in a quadratic-character family and explains that very small nonzero central values remain possible despite positivity and nonvanishing questions.
accepted_units.context_note: The source later restricts the proof to discriminants of the form 8d without claiming that restriction is the full theorem statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponential constants and fractions are vulnerable to extraction damage and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Cusp-form central values and the functional-equation parity obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the Hecke eigenform family and its L-functions, identifies the parity class in which the functional equation forces central vanishing, and states large and small central-value results in the non-forced-zero class.
accepted_units.context_note: The harmonic weighting and trace-formula implementation appear in Section 4.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions are readable; displayed Fourier/L-series formulas and the exact asymptotic scale need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Optimization depth versus portability of resonance
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the optimized zeta application from deliberately simplified family applications and records that longer resonators could improve constants; it also identifies resonance as portable to character sums, zeta derivatives at zeros, and eigenfunction norms.
accepted_units.context_note: Applications cited as other or ongoing work are scope evidence, not proofs supplied by this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded, except the extracted replacement constant on line 187 should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Fourier diagonalization of smoothed zeta resonance moments
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the resonator norm and zeta-mixed moment, uses rapid Fourier decay plus the length condition to suppress off-diagonal frequencies, and reduces the analytic problem to an explicit coefficient quotient.
accepted_units.context_note: The truncated Dirichlet-series approximation for zeta and the condition N at most T to a fixed power below one are essential to the reduction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy text-layer extraction; exact summation constraints, powers, conjugations, and error terms require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Sparse multiplicative resonator for the lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: States the extremal quotient scale and constructs a squarefree-supported multiplicative resonator concentrated on a prime window. Rankin's trick turns the finite cutoff into a negligible Euler-product tail, leaving a product whose linear prime terms generate the large exponential gain.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves the lower half of the finite optimization theorem, not yet the zeta theorem itself.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The coefficient window, auxiliary parameter, Euler products, and error exponent are formula-sensitive and need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Multiplicative majorant limiting every resonator
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a multiplicative weight g and applies a two-term quadratic inequality to dominate every numerator by the coefficient norm times two tractable divisor sums, establishing that arbitrary coefficients cannot beat the stated resonance scale.
accepted_units.context_note: This complements the explicit construction in the preceding unit and explains the optimality internal to the chosen quotient problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact definition of g, divisor sums, and logarithmic error term require verification against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: From the optimized quotient to a zeta maximum and moderate-value frequency
accepted_units.why_material: Substitutes the optimization theorem into the resonant quotient for the maximum, then uses the second and fourth moments of zeta with Cauchy-Schwarz to force a nontrivial measure of moderately large values.
accepted_units.context_note: The frequency argument here covers the lower V regime; larger V requires the redesigned resonator in the next unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The threshold and logarithmic powers in the moment calculation are formula-dependent and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: High-threshold frequency from a resonator and fourth-moment control
accepted_units.why_material: Turns a mixed moment exceeding twice the thresholded norm into a lower bound for the large-value set via two Cauchy applications, then chooses a shorter prime-supported resonator so its fourth moment diagonalizes and tunes its scale parameter to the desired threshold.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a different optimization objective from the pointwise-maximal resonator and depends on the fourth resonator moment as a concentration penalty.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy extraction; the resonator support, fourth-moment product, parameter relation, and final exponent all require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic-character resonator and square detection
accepted_units.why_material: Defines family moments over squarefree discriminants and a character-valued resonator. Expanding its norm shows that character orthogonality is replaced by a square/non-square dichotomy, with perfect-square products supplying the main term and character-sum estimates controlling the rest.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses a restricted discriminant subfamily sufficient for existence; the subsequent mixed moment additionally needs an approximate functional equation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Legendre/Kronecker symbols, square conditions, local factors, and error exponents need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Approximate functional equation and the quadratic-family mixed moment
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a smoothed approximate functional equation to expose an extra character variable, then applies the same square detector to derive an asymptotic mixed moment whose main term is supported exactly when the product of three indices is an odd square.
accepted_units.context_note: The weight's small- and large-argument behavior justifies truncation and partial summation; the main term is simplified later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong formula dependency: Mellin definition of the weight, derivative bounds, square constraint, integral, and error estimates require PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: One multiplicative profile selects either small or large quadratic central values
accepted_units.why_material: States asymptotics for the resonator norm and mixed moment in which using mu times f produces negative linear Euler factors and an exponentially small quotient, while removing mu reverses the effect and gives large values.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposition is established in lines 691-863; this span contains both the asymptotic mechanism and its extremal consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prime product signs and the exact N versus X restriction are essential and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Rankin control of the quadratic resonator norm
accepted_units.why_material: Extends a truncated squarefree multiplicative sum to an Euler product and uses a small Rankin exponent to prove that the omitted tail and character-sum error remain negligible in the permitted length range.
accepted_units.context_note: This reuses the zeta-section cutoff technique in a family-specific norm with extra local density factors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponents, local p over p-plus-one factor, and admissible length range require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Parametrizing the square constraint and extracting the quadratic mixed-moment residue
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes the two resonator indices into their gcd and coprime parts, parametrizes the square-condition variable accordingly, Mellin-inverts its weighted sum, and moves contour to extract the zeta pole. This converts an opaque square constraint into a multiplicative main term with an explicit logarithmic factor.
accepted_units.context_note: The extraction is source-recoverable at the architectural level, but individual factors are not safe to transplant without the PDF.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula and symbol-order dependency; gcd variables, powers, local products, contour locations, and residue terms require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Euler factorization and tail completion of the quadratic mixed moment
accepted_units.why_material: Extends the constrained coprime sums to all indices, factors the extension prime by prime, simplifies harmless local weights, and applies Rankin's trick to show that the extension tails are exponentially smaller than the main product.
accepted_units.context_note: Together with the preceding residue unit this proves the mixed-moment half of Proposition 3.3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact Euler factors and tail ratios are formula-sensitive and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Harmonic Petersson weights turn the cusp-form family into a diagonal norm
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces harmonic weights, applies Petersson's trace formula, and uses a small-argument Bessel bound plus a resonator-length restriction to make off-diagonal Kloosterman contributions exponentially small, leaving the coefficient square norm.
accepted_units.context_note: The weights are roughly constant, allowing a later weighted-family average to imply existence of an individual form.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Normalizations, trace-formula constants, Bessel range, and length bounds require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Approximate functional equation for cusp-form central values
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the central-value expansion by contour shifting and the functional equation, including the parity factor that annihilates the forced-zero class, and records weight estimates that make the Dirichlet series effectively short.
accepted_units.context_note: This prepares the mixed family moment; it does not by itself choose a resonator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour formula, gamma ratios, parity factor, and the two weight estimates require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Hecke multiplication and Petersson averaging yield a gcd kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the approximate functional equation with Hecke relations and Petersson orthogonality to reduce the central-value-weighted resonator average to a finite quadratic form with kernel sigma of the gcd divided by the geometric mean.
accepted_units.context_note: The shortness conditions on both resonator and central-value expansion are what keep the trace formula effectively diagonal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Hecke relation indices, weight replacement, gcd divisor sum, and error term are formula-sensitive and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Mobius twisting switches large to small cusp-form central values
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the norm and gcd-kernel quadratic form with the same multiplicative profile used in the zeta optimization; positive coefficients create reinforcing linear Euler factors for large values, while multiplying by mu reverses them to produce small values.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the final family-specific realization of the paper's common resonance template.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact products, constants, and admissible N choice require PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A common resonance quotient across three spectral settings
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: In each setting, a tailored orthogonality mechanism converts a resonator norm and a central-value mixed moment into two finite quadratic forms; an unusually large or small ratio forces an extreme member of the averaging domain.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The diagonalizing inputs differ substantially—Fourier decay in t, quadratic-character square detection, and Petersson-Hecke averaging—so the source does not establish an abstract theorem covering arbitrary families.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Coefficient signs as an extremal-direction control
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same prime-supported magnitude profile can select large or small central values because a Mobius sign twist reverses the linear prime contributions in the mixed-moment Euler product while leaving the norm essentially unchanged.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This paired sign mechanism is demonstrated for the quadratic-character and cusp-form families; the zeta section proves large values only.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Diagonal extraction is limited by representation length
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The useful resonator length is set by the point at which the chosen analytic representation still suppresses off-diagonal terms; changing from a second to a fourth resonator moment or from zeta to a family changes that length budget.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source supplies setting-specific inequalities and does not claim these displayed length bounds are universally optimal.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Rankin's trick as the finite-to-multiplicative bridge
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across the constructions, Rankin weighting certifies that extending length-truncated nonnegative or absolute majorant sums to Euler products loses negligibly little, making primewise coefficient design analytically usable.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The tail estimates depend on the particular coefficient support, positivity or majorization, and parameter ranges in each application.

within_source_saturation: The plan represents every source-local theorem target, conceptual bridge, distinct diagonalization mechanism, coefficient-design argument, extremal-direction switch, and nonroutine truncation or concentration device. Unselected lines are front matter, historical or transition context already attached to units, page furniture, blanks, or bibliography; further segmentation would predominantly isolate routine algebraic steps or repeat mechanisms already represented.
stop_reason: The source ends after the cusp-form sign-switch conclusion at line 1042, followed only by references and author contact information through line 1077. All three applications of resonance and all proof-specific mechanisms that differ across them have been captured, so no meaningful unrepresented source material remains.
